title: Engine Controls — Fire Handle Replacement with a Distinct Second Discharge Detent
abstract: Replacement of both engine fire handles by an assembly with a positive detent and a separate illuminated legend at the second discharge position, offered for training commonality rather than as an airworthiness action.

sections.planning_reason: Operator training departments report that during the engine fire drill crews frequently cannot tell from the handle whether the second discharge has been selected, because the two positions differ by about eight millimetres of travel and share one legend. Four line events were recorded where the second bottle was discharged unintentionally during the first drill step and two where it was not discharged when the procedure called for it. A regulator asked for the ambiguity to be addressed after reviewing the fleet training records, without raising an airworthiness finding.
sections.description: The bulletin replaces both fire handle assemblies with units carrying a positive detent between the first and second discharge positions and a separate illuminated legend for each, and separates the two discharge circuits back to the handle.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Safety the fire extinguishing bottles and fit the discharge inhibit pins. Open the flight compartment pedestal. Remove both fire handle assemblies. Rework the firewall panel CID171471-49 behind the pedestal locally for the deeper unit and re-protect the machined area. Install the seal HOD830120-93 behind each escutcheon. Install the new handle assemblies and torque the bolts AES254025-97. Re-terminate the two discharge circuits at functional items 47EC and 596EC so that they are separated back to the handle, and connect the position feedback at functional item 33EC. Do the installation task AMM-C-76-20-11-400-021-A. Do the legend illumination check and the discharge circuit continuity check with the bottles still safetied, and record the results. Remove the inhibit pins and restore the bottles. Close the pedestal and record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to CIRRANE-11 and CIRRANE-13 aircraft from MSN C00205 to MSN C00796 that carry the delivered handle. Aircraft from MSN C00796 onward are already at the standard. Both handles must be changed together so that the two engines behave identically.
sections.material_note: Kit K7620-2005-01 contains two handle assemblies, the seals, the fastener set and the legend caps. Lead time is twenty-two weeks. Removed handles are returned to the supplier under the exchange agreement.

type_data.compliance_time: At the operator's convenience. Operators seeking fleet-wide training commonality are advised to plan a single campaign.
